item.text: I’m reviewing the current implementation for the next refactor seam instead of doing more local churn. The main weakness now is that tree mutation logic is still split between `AVLTree` and `Node`, even though most of the balancing mechanics are node-local concerns.

I’ve confirmed the next worthwhile step: move structural mutation down into `Node` so the outer tree class stops micromanaging rotations and balance maintenance. That will reduce the private surface area on `AVLTree` and keep subtree operations with the type they actually mutate.
The mutation logic is now node-local. I’m compiling and running the demo to confirm the refactor preserved behavior before I summarize it.
The behavior stayed stable. I’m pulling line references now so the summary can point directly to the node-local mutation changes.

Further refactored [AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:53) so subtree mutation now lives with `Node` instead of being split across the outer tree class.

The main change is that insertion, rebalancing, and rotations are now node-local static operations at [AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:80). `AVLTree.insert(...)` became a thin coordinator that validates input, delegates to `Node.insert(...)`, and updates `size` from the recorded mutation state ([AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:167)). That removed a chunk of private tree-level plumbing and tightened cohesion around the data structure’s structural invariants.

I also simplified lookup slightly by comparing directly through the stored comparator in `contains(...)` at [AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:180), since the outer `compare(...)` helper is no longer needed.

Verification: `javac AVLTree.java AVLTreeDemo.java` succeeded, and `java AVLTreeDemo` still prints `30 20 10 25 40 50`.
